title: Integrating factor formula
text: For $$y'+p\left(x\right) y=q(x)$$, the integrating factor is $$\mu(x)=\exp\left(\int{p(x)}\, dx\right)$$ which means $$e$$ raised to the integral of $$p(x)$$ with no constant of integration needed.

title: Find $$p(x)$$
text: In standard form the equation is $$y'-x y=3$$, so $$p(x)=-x$$. Its integral is $$\frac{-x^2}{2}$$, so the integrating factor is $$e^{\left(-\frac{x^2}{2}\right)}$$.
